subject: Post-demo: proposed evaluation sprint & success guardrails
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Sara Jones <sara.jones@atlas-systems.com>, Tom Liu <tom.liu@atlas-systems.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Jul 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: proposed evaluation sprint & success guardrails

Thanks again for your time this morning — appreciate the candid discussion about the search assistant workflows and the latency/cost constraints you called out. Per our demo, I captured a concise proposed evaluation sprint below so Atlas can validate performance, integration effort, and cost impact without a wide rollout.

High-level objective:
- Validate Redwood inference can meet Atlas’ 95th percentile latency <= 250ms for 1k qps mixed load and deliver expected relevance uplift on the Search Assistant intent set.

Proposed 3-week evaluation sprint (owners & checkpoints):
1) Week 0 (prep, 2 business days) — Data ingestion + access
   - Atlas: provide sample query logs (anonymized) and 1–2 representative prompt templates (owner: Tom).
   - Redwood: provide S3 ingestion spec and sample ingestion scripts (owner: Marissa).
2) Week 1 (integration & baseline) — 5 business days
   - Redwood: deploy a dedicated trial instance, run baseline model (open model v1), collect latency/CPS metrics, provide an initial relevance sample set (owner: Karthik).
   - Atlas: run smoke tests against staging endpoints, confirm auth/KMS (owner: Sara).
3) Week 2 (optimization & evaluation) — 5 business days
   - Redwood: apply batching/quantization profile and KV cache rules suggested for your query distribution; re-run perf/relevance tests (owner: Karthik).
   - Atlas: provide 100 labeled queries for automated quality regression checks (owner: Tom).
4) Week 3 (review & decision) — 3 business days
   - Joint review of performance, cost delta, and qualitative pass/fail on success criteria. Recommend go/no-go meeting. (owner: Irene/Atlas PD lead).

Success criteria (pass = all must be met):
- Perf: 95th percentile latency <= 250ms under mixed load approximating 1k qps.
- Quality: >10% relative improvement on relevance metric (MRR@5) vs current baseline on provided holdout set.
- Effort: engineering integration time <= 3 FTE-days from Atlas side for baseline connect.
- Cost: projected per-100k query cost < 50% increase over your current infra (we'll provide an itemized projection).

Deliverables I attached:
- atlas-poc-template.pdf — sprint checklist and tech acceptance rubric.
- demo-recording-20260717.mp4 — full recording with timestamps.

Next steps / asks:
- Can Atlas confirm the two owners (stated above) and a kickoff window next week? Preferred kickoff: Tue 07/21 or Wed 07/22.
- Share a small anonymized sample of search logs (500–2k rows) by end of day Monday so we can pre-stage ingestion scripts.

I'll loop Marissa in as your Redwood engagement lead for the sprint; she'll coordinate the engineering checklist and daily 15-min syncs. If anything here needs to change, please call it out and we'll adapt.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198
Redwood Inference

From: Sara Jones <sara.jones@atlas-systems.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Liu <tom.liu@atlas-systems.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Jul 2026 12:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: proposed evaluation sprint & success guardrails

Irene — thanks, this is very clear and helpful. We like the short sprint approach and the specific pass/fail guardrails. A few clarifying questions before we lock dates: 

1) For the latency measurement, what exact traffic profile should we emulate so your 1k qps statement is comparable to our production mix? Can you share the load generator config?
2) For ">10% relative improvement" — can you confirm which relevance metric Redwood plans to use (MRR@5 is fine) and how you handle synonyms/partial matches?
3) On data sharing: we can provide anonymized logs. We'll need a short DPIA / data handling note for our legal team describing retention & deletion timelines for the sample data.

Owners: confirmed — Tom will own the sample logs and engineering validation; I'll own scheduling and procurement touches.

Kickoff preferences: Wed 07/22 looks best for us (am PST). Can you do 9:30am?

Thanks — Sara
Sara Jones
Director of Search Engineering, Atlas Systems
sara.jones@atlas-systems.com | (212) 555-0122

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sara Jones <sara.jones@atlas-systems.com>, Tom Liu <tom.liu@atlas-systems.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 08:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: proposed evaluation sprint & success guardrails

Sara — great questions. Quick answers and what we'll share ahead of the kickoff: 

1) Traffic profile: we'll provide a JMeter config that mirrors a 70/20/10 percentile split for short/medium/long queries and the exact timing parameters we used in the demo. I'll attach the load generator config and a simple Docker command to run it.

2) Metric: we'll measure MRR@5 and NDCG@10. For synonyms/partial matches we use a fuzzy-match tolerance at the scorer stage and will share the scoring script (python snippet) so you can reproduce locally. We will also include an evaluation harness that runs on your labeled set.

3) DPIA/data handling: Marissa will share a short data handling statement (S3 retention 7 days, immediate deletion on request, sample set hashed/anonymized) and our SOC2 reference. For the sprint we keep all sample artifacts in a customer-scoped bucket and provide an audit log.

Attachments we will push to the shared Drive before kickoff:
- loadgen-jmeter-config.json (example)
- redwood-eval-harness.tar.gz
- redwood-dpia-statement.pdf

Operational notes:
- Cost projection: final line-item by end of Week 1 after baseline run.
- Escalation: if performance regresses >20% in Week 2 we'll enable a canary fallback and schedule a technical deep-dive.

Confirming kickoff: Wed, 2026-07-22 09:30 AM PDT works for the Redwood team.

Karthik Iyer
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0137
